archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (below-average 5-on-5)
archetype.definition: A team whose ugly goal differential is inflated by 8.6% shooting and a 65.5% penalty kill that should both recover, but whose 47.2% share of expected goals says the recovery lands it short of .500, not back in the race.

report.headline: Bad luck explains some of 2-5-2; the five-on-five slide explains the rest.
report.take:
Nine games in, the Kings sit 2-5-2, 30th of 32 on the site, with a goal differential per game of -1.22 that ranks 28th. They score 2.33 goals a game, 29th, against a league rate of 3.15, and allow 3.56. The opening six-game losing streak set the tone, and the 2-3-0 run since has only partly repaired it. On pace this is a 55-point team. It is not that bad, but the honest correction is smaller than the record's ugliness suggests.

Two things are dragging the scoreboard below the underlying play. The skaters are shooting 8.6% in all situations, 28th, against a league average of 11.3%, while the shot volume is ordinary: 27.2 a game against a league 27.4. Then the penalty kill has stopped only 65.5% of power plays, 31st, where the league kills 78.3%. Neither number is likely to hold at that level, and the 5-on-5 PDO of 97.9 says the even-strength finishing is running cold too. The goaltending is not stealing anything either. Team GSAx is -3.5, and both Darcy Kuemper (-1.1) and Anton Forsberg (-1.0) are below expected. There is no close-game luck to blame: Pts vs Goal Diff is -0.4, about neutral, with the one-goal losses to Florida and Vegas offset by the overtime win on Long Island.

What the regression story can't fix is the trend under it. The Kings' 5-on-5 expected-goals share was 55.2% two seasons ago, 52.4% last year and 47.2% now, 22nd. The shot-attempt share of 49% is closer to even, so the puck is there but the chances are thinner. Last year's 90 points also leaned on 5.6 points beyond the goal differential, so that team was already weaker than its record. The grades are D- up front, F on the blue line and D- in goal. The top of the lineup is fine: Artemi Panarin has 6 goals with a 54.7% xGF, Adrian Kempe is at 55.5%, Brandt Clarke at 61.4% and Quinton Byfield at 62%. The problem is everyone the coach has to play behind them. Drew Doughty (38.6%), Brian Dumoulin (38.4%), Erik Haula (33.6%) and Mats Zuccarello (31.3%) are getting buried, and they carry heavy minutes.

The direction from here is up, because the shooting and the kill will normalize, but not far. Against this schedule's soft spots the Kings should look like a team in the high 70s in points, not one chasing a playoff spot. The offense ranked 29th last season too, so the scoring drought is not all bad bounces.

strengths.title: The top wingers are producing
strengths.body: Panarin has 6 goals and 9 points and Kempe 8 points, and both are winning their 5-on-5 minutes at 54.7% and 55.5% expected goals. Their production has come despite a team that can't finish, so it should hold. This is the one part of the lineup playing like the 2024-25 team.

strengths.title: Clarke and Byfield drive play
strengths.body: Brandt Clarke is the lone bright spot on an F-graded blue line: 7 points, a 61.4% xGF and 35th of 250 on the defense tab. Byfield's 62% xGF is the best among the forwards even with a -6 that reflects the cold goaltending behind him. These are process numbers, and they tend to translate into points once the shooting turns.

strengths.title: Possession is close to even
strengths.body: The 49% shot-attempt share ranks 17th, and shots for a game sit right at the league average. A team that holds the puck this often and shoots 8.6% is due for more goals. That gives the recovery a real floor, even if the chance quality limits its ceiling.

concerns.title: A penalty kill in free fall
concerns.body: At 65.5% the kill ranks 31st, far under the league's 78.3%. Part of that is a nine-game sample and goalies running below expected. But the kill was already down to 74.6% last season from 81.4% the year before, so the slide predates this October. Expect it to climb back toward the mid-70s, not to where it was.

concerns.title: The depth is getting buried
concerns.body: Behind the top players, the minutes go to skaters losing badly at 5-on-5. Doughty plays nearly 21 minutes a night at a 38.6% xGF, Dumoulin is at 38.4% and Mikey Anderson at 42.7%, which is why the blue line grades an F. Up front, Haula (33.6%) and Zuccarello (31.3%, 123rd of 124 wingers) drag the forward grade to D-. Bounces won't fix this, and it is what pulls the team's xGF down to 47.2%.

concerns.title: The scoring problem isn't new
concerns.body: It's tempting to blame the 29th-ranked offense on the 8.6% shooting, and some of it is that. But the Kings were 29th in offense last season too, and the power play has gone from 17.9% two years ago to 14.8% now. Shooting regression adds goals, not a new identity.

trend.note: A six-game losing streak to open, then a modest steadying: over the last five, goals allowed per game are down by 0.56 against the season rate and the differential is better by 0.42. The record over that stretch is still 2-3-0, and it has come on the road.

weekAhead.headline: Chicago and Buffalo offer points; New York and Ottawa won't.
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with a road back-to-back, at the Rangers and then at Chicago, before two home games against Ottawa and Buffalo. The Rangers and Senators are the hard half. New York is 9th on the site with an A- in goal, a .909 save percentage and a 92.3% penalty kill, the worst possible draw for a power play at 14.8%. Ottawa allows only 23.3 shots a game, 5th, and wins on a 103 PDO.

The other half is exactly what a cold-shooting team needs. Chicago is 31st on the site with a 40.3% xGF and a .880 save percentage. Buffalo's goaltending grades an F with a league-worst .866, and its forwards give up the second-most points over expectation in the league. A split of four games is the floor. Taking both soft games and stealing one of the others would be the first real sign the shooting is turning.

keyMatchups.title: Clarke against Chicago's leaky blue line
keyMatchups.body: Chicago allows defensemen 1.21 points a game more than expected, the worst rate in the league, and 30.8% of the points it gives up go to defensemen. Clarke and Gustafsson are the Kings' only productive defensemen. The second night of a back-to-back is a good spot for them to add to their totals.

keyMatchups.title: Wingers against Ottawa and Buffalo
keyMatchups.body: Ottawa gives wingers 0.64 points a game over expectation (28th), and Buffalo 1.12 (31st). That plays directly to the Kings' strength, with Panarin, Kempe and Laferriere all on the wing. Buffalo's .866 save percentage makes Saturday the likeliest night for the finishing to break out.

keyMatchups.title: A broken kill meets weak power plays
keyMatchups.body: The 65.5% kill gets a break this week. Chicago's power play is last at 8.3%, Buffalo's 31st at 10.5% and Ottawa's 29th at 11.5%. If the Kings still leak power-play goals against these units, the problem is structural, not variance.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the penalty kill holds against three of the league's four worst power plays; that tells you if 65.5% is noise.

restOfSeason.body:
From here the Kings should be better than their pace, which the sheet puts at 55 points. Shooting at 8.6% against an 11.3% league average won't last for a team with league-average shot volume, and a 65.5% kill should drift up. Average goaltending alone would erase much of the -3.5 GSAx hole. Those corrections point to a final total of roughly 72-82 points and 30-36 wins, with scoring settling around 2.7-3.0 goals a game.

What caps the climb is the 5-on-5 game. A 47.2% expected-goals share is a below-average team's number, and it has fallen three seasons running. The minutes the coach gives to Doughty, Dumoulin, Anderson, Haula and Zuccarello are the reason, and better luck doesn't change that. The team the Kings regress toward is a sub-.500 one, which is too far behind in a Pacific led by Edmonton and Vegas to matter in the standings.

projections.stat: Goals scored / game, rest of season

swingFactors: Penalty kill recovering toward league average
Kuemper and Forsberg reaching league-average saves
The depth defensemen and forwards stopping the 5-on-5 bleeding

confidence.note: Nine games; shooting, save and kill rates are all small-sample, though the multi-year xGF slide is not.
